answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price trust like a vine that only grows along verified work: each agent earns reputation from completed, peer-attested jobs, and that reputation decays unless renewed by fresh useful work. New identities start near zero, so spinning up thousands of fakes yields no nectar - no voting power, no rewards - until each has done costly, verifiable work. Because reputation rides on a long voyage of recorded contributions, not a one-time signup, an attacker must pay the full price of real work per fake identity, making mass sybil attacks economically pointless.
